You will see Liberty Square and Avenida 18 de Julio, then reach Independence Square, with its monument to José Artigas and Palacio Salvo. Nearby stands the Gateway of the Citadel, a surviving section of the colonial-era fortifications.

The route continues along pedestrianized Sarandí Street through Ciudad Vieja. Highlights include the Metropolitan Cathedral (Iglesia Matriz), the monument to city founder Bruno Mauricio de Zabala, and Solís Theatre, one of South America's notable historic theaters.

lead: After breakfast, set out on a private trip to Vicente Pérez Rosales National Park in the heart of Chile's Lake District.
  The route passes through evergreen forests, mountain scenery, and crystal-clear lakes. The main stop is Petrohué Falls,
  where turquoise water rushes over dark volcanic rock. The contrast of black lava, bright green vegetation, and powerful

As you walk along maintained trails, you can admire the Petrohué River, take photographs, and enjoy views of ancient forests, mountain peaks, and volcanic landscapes. The journey then continues to Osorno Volcano, one of Chile's symbols. In clear weather, there are impressive views of its snow-covered summit and the surrounding lakes. Return to Puerto Varas in the evening.

## Water and Forests of the Lake District

In southern Chile, water, forests, and mountains shape the landscape. Petrohué Falls show this scenery in motion: water races through a rocky channel, foams over the stones, and gathers again into a fast-flowing river. It is a place to linger by the water and watch the changing colors and patterns of the current.

Peulla lies on the eastern shore of Todos los Santos Lake, surrounded by mountains and green slopes. The village is connected to Petrohué by boat; the lake between them becomes an important part of discovering the region. The surrounding area is known for nature walks and small waterfalls, while additional activities are selected separately under the terms of the trip.

The excursion brings together Peulla and Petrohué and appeals to lovers of lakeside scenery. Even a short stop by the water can be memorable: the sound of rushing water, cool air, and reflections of the forest. For southern Chile, a light waterproof jacket and shoes suitable for walking on wet surfaces are useful.

## Excursion Terms

The excursion costs $103 per person.

Discounts may be available for more than one person; contact us to discuss.
